sentences.text:
By the impugned judgment and order of conviction, 5 th Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Jamnagar, vide its judgment and order dated 21.04.2022 passed in Criminal Case No. 1989 of 2011 was pleased to NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/1001/2022 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined convict the respondent nos.2 to 8 herein only for the offence punishable under Section 465, 471, 120(B) of IPC, whereby respondent nos.2 to 8 are convicted under Section 465 of IPC for a period of one year Simple Imprisonment and fine of Rs.2000/- and in default of payment of fine further Simple Imprisonment of 3 months was awarded.

The respondent nos.2 to 8 were also convicted for the offences punishable u/s 471 for the period of 1 year Simple Imprisonment and fine of Rs. 2000/- and in default of payment of fine further Simple Imprisonment of 3 months was awarded.

The respondent nos.2 to 8 were also convicted for the offence punishable under Section 120(B) for the period of 6 months Simple Imprisonment and fine of Rs. 500/- and in default of payment of fine further Simple Imprisonment of 1 month was awarded.
The respondent nos.2 to 8 though also convicted for the offence under Section 34 of IPC, however, no sentence is awarded qua said offence.
The learned Magistrate has also ordered to run all punishment concurrently.
So far as other charges of offence punishable under Sections 467, 468, 474 & 420 of IPC are concerned, the respondent nos.2 to 8 are acquitted.

3. It would be appropriate to mention at this stage that against the order of conviction, the respondents herein have preferred an appeal being Criminal Appeal No.130 of 2022 filed and pending before 2 nd NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/1001/2022 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined Additional Sessions Judge, Jamanagar.

4. The applicant herein has also filed an appeal against acquittal being Criminal Appeal No.501 of 2023 as the trial Court had recorded acquittal for some of the sections for which also the respondents were tried.

5. The earlier bench of this Court had passed an order in Criminal Appeal No.501 of 2023 referring to the present revision in its order dated 19.06.2023 and accordingly, by the office submission, the then Acting Chief Justice ordered the revision application to be heard with the Criminal Appeal against acquittal.
This Court today by a separate order has disposed of the Criminal Appeal against the acquittal by rejecting the same.

6. Learned advocate for the applicant has submitted that once the trial Judge has found the respondents guilty of intentionally forging the documents, the learned Judge ought to have awarded the maximum sentence prescribed, and there is no justification for awarding sentence of one year only of Simple Imprisonment.

sentences.text: Learned advocate has therefore, taken this Court to Exh document produced as evidence before the Civil Court and submitted that the entire premise of the civil suit was this forged document which the trial Court gave a finding as having been forged and therefore, the trial Judge had no option but to inflict maximum sentence.

Learned advocate also took this Court through evidence of independent witness Exh.147, the stamp vendor and submitted that by evidence on record the case of the forged document was proved beyond doubt against the respondents also that there was conspiracy in forging the document, still the punishment awarded is only to the extent of six months for Section 120(B) of IPC.
6.2. Learned advocate has argued that only reason assigned by the trial Judge to award a lesser sentence is the advance age of the respondents.

It is submitted that the Apex Court in its judgment in case of State of Rajasthan v/s. Mehram and others reported in AIR 2020 SC 2089 has not accepted the proposition of advanced age to award the lesser sentence.

sentences.text: 7. Learned advocate for the respondents has argued that the trial Judge has assigned cogent reasons to impose the sentence and it is always the discretion of the trial Court to impose the sentence with due NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/1001/2022 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined regard to the attending circumstance and in present case, the trial Judge has rightly exercised the discretion with due regard to the nature of offense as well as the age and social status of the respondents-accused.

7.1 It is further submitted that the revision need not be entertained as the appeal against the conviction itself is pending before the appellate Court and in the event of the acquittal of the respondents in the appeal, the entire exercise will be rendered fruitless.
8. Heard learned advocates for the parties and perused the documents placed on record.

The Court may at the outset refer to the judgment of the Apex Court in case of State of Punjab v/s. Prem Sagar and others reported in 2008 (7) SCC 550, wherein para-8, the Court has held as under:-
"8.

entities.text: State of Punjab v/s. Prem Sagar and others reported in 2008 (7) SCC 550
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although a wide discretion has been conferred upon the court, the same must be exercised judiciously.
It would depend upon the circumstances in which the crime has been committed and his mental state.
Age of the accused is also relevant."
8.1 The sentencing is therefore, an independent exercise to be undertaken by the trial Court upon recording the conviction.
Thereafter, guided by several principles and procedure laid down, the trial Court proceeded to impose the sentence.

The Court has thereafter taken into consideration the facts that the convicts were not habitual offenders.
The issue arose out of a land transaction where civil proceedings were going on.
Lastly, the trial Court has also considered a relevant circumstance that some of the respondents are ladies and all are of old age.

8.3 The Court has therefore applied the principle of law laid down in case of Shyam Narain v/s.

8.4 The trial Court has thereafter exercised its discretion while considering the background of the respondents, their social and financial status and the age of the respondents to inflict the lesser sentence.

8.5 The conviction recorded by the trial Court for offense of forgery under Section 463 of IPC and the punishment is provided under Section 465 of IPC where maximum sentence provided is imprisonment of either NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/1001/2022 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined description for a term which may extent to two years or fine or both.

Section 471 of the IPC provides for the punishment is same manner as Section 465 of IPC again for two years maximum, whereas for offense under Section 120(B) of the IPC, the punishment inflicted is of six months Simple Imprisonment.

8.6 While exercising discretion by assigning cogent reasons, for such exercise has inflicted sentence of Simple Imprisonment of one year for offense under Sections 465 and 471 of IPC, while six months of Section 120(B) of IPC.
8.7 The reliance placed on the decision of the Apex Court in case of State of Rajasthan (supra).

sentences.text:
In this case, the Court has considered the contention regarding advanced age to observe as under:-
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/1001/2022 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined "13.

The learned counsel for the accused No. 5 was at pains to persuade us that the said accused is now about 7075 years of age and at this distance of time, it may not be appropriate to send him back to jail.
Taking overall view of the matter, we are not impressed by this submission.

Even in case of offence under Section 326, IPC,
which commended to the High Court, the same was punishable with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment of either description which may extend to ten years and also liable to fine.
Had it been a conviction under Section 326, as aforesaid, the sentence of only about five months in the facts of the present case, by no stretch of imagination, was adequate."
9. Concerning what is recorded by the learned trial Judge in its order imposing sentence, the Court finds no reason to interfere with the sentence imposed by the trial Court.
Hence, Criminal Revision Application stands rejected.
Notice is discharged.
